html:
The Arosaguntacook, or Androscoggin, were an Abenaki people of the Northeastern Woodlands. They lived along the Androscoggin River in what are now Maine and New Hampshire, farming maize in the river valleys, fishing and hunting.

They were part of the wider Wabanaki world and allies of New France. In the wars between New England and New France from the 1670s to the 1750s, English settlers moving up the coast and rivers took their land. By the 1700s they had been absorbed into neighbouring tribes and moved north to the Saint-François mission at Odanak in Quebec, where Abenaki communities live today. Their neighbours included the Pennacook.
